stem: Which of the following is the solution set of the inequality \(-4(x - 2) \ge 2x - 10\)?
solution: Divide by \(-6\) and reverse the inequality sign: \(x \le 3\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This forgets to reverse the inequality sign when dividing both sides by the negative number \(-6\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of distributing incorrectly, \(-4x - 8\) instead of \(-4x + 8\), which gives \(-6x \ge -2\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This drops a negative sign at the end: \(-6x \ge -18\) gives \(x \le 3\), not \(x \le -3\).
explanation.D: Correct. \(-4x + 8 \ge 2x - 10\) gives \(-6x \ge -18\); dividing by \(-6\) reverses the sign, so \(x \le 3\).

verify:
rel = lambda s: value(s.replace('\\le', '<=').replace('\\ge', '>='))

x = symbols('x')
s = solve_univariate_inequality(-4*(x - 2) >= 2*x - 10, x, relational=False)
assert s == Interval(-oo, 3)
ok = [k for k in choices if rel(choices[k]).as_set() == s]
assert ok == [answer]
